result.title: Fix the Match, Not the Solver: STITCH -- a Self-Supervised Compatibility Measure for Eroded Visual Puzzles
result.summary: Unlike the clean and pixel-aligned complete pieces of standard jigsaw benchmarks, real-world puzzle fragments lose their boundary regions to erosion, destroying the signal that classical compatibility measures (CMs) rely on. We first re-establish, via oracle experiments, that the CM, not the solver, is the performance bottleneck: with a perfect CM, even a simple greedy solver achieves perfect reconstruction. This motivates STITCH, a self-supervised CM that sidesteps missing boundaries by comparing frozen ViT patch tokens from piece interiors via a lightweight cross-attention head (~249K trainable parameters), trained without manual annotation. Plugged into unchanged compatibility-based solvers, STITCH reaches .992/.954 Abs/Perf on JPwLEG-5 (+.629 Perf over the best prior method), nearly saturating the benchmark. On a new ImageNet 7x7 benchmark, it outperforms all alternatives, including inpaint-then-match pipelines built on modern generative models. Importantly, performance remains robust across erosion levels and generalizes to puzzles with over 40% missing pieces without retraining. Trained on the recent GAP datasets of irregular, heavily eroded fragments, the same CM recipe enables compatibility-based solvers to surpass recent learning-based solvers on GAP-3 and GAP-5. Since this leap in performance is achieved by a pluggable CM module, the takeaway is clear: fix the match, not the solver.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对碎片边界被侵蚀的视觉拼图，先用 oracle 实验论证瓶颈在相容性度量而非求解器，进而提出自监督 STITCH：用冻结 ViT 的碎片内部 patch token 经轻量 cross-attention 头（约 249K 可训练参数）判断相容性，插入原有求解器后在多个基准上大幅提升，并对不同程度的缺失保持稳健。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「冻结 ViT patch token + 轻量 cross-attention 比较内部区域」以及「瓶颈在匹配表示而非求解器」的诊断，可能为核查 LVR 中视觉细节是否留在内部状态、latent 表示与推理模块孰为瓶颈提供借鉴线索；但任务域（拼图重排）与多模态推理相距较远，可供人工核查。
